Wind is the more plausible driver. Meridional wind at 10m carries moisture and heat into the region, which changes cloud water. The data show a moderate positive correlation between the two (r ≈ 0.32), but correlation alone can't give direction, so I chose B on physical reasoning rather than a causal-discovery test. Cloud water is also unlikely to drive near-surface winds directly. I didn't test for causal direction, for example with conditional-independence or non-Gaussianity methods.

ANSWER: B
